question.problem:
Given the joint probability distribution for two discrete random variables $X$ and $Y$ below, find $\text{E}[2X-3Y].$

| $f$ | $Y=2$ | $Y=3$ |
| --- | --- | --- |
| $X=1$ | $0.25$ | $0.1$ |
| $X=2$ | $0.2$ | $0.15$ |
| $X=4$ | $0.15$ | $0.15$ |
question.worked_solution:
Recall that the marginal distribution for $X$ corresponds to the row totals, and the marginal distribution for $Y$ corresponds to the column totals. | $f$ | $Y=2$ | $Y=3$ | ${f}_{X}$ | | --- | --- | --- | --- | | $X=1$ | $0.25$ | $0.1$ | $0.35$ | | $X=2$ | $0.2$ | $0.15$ | $0.35$ | | $X=4$ | $0.15$ | $0.15$ | $0.3$ | | ${f}_{Y}$ | $0.6$ | $0.4$ | $1$ | Therefore, the probability mass functions for $X$ and $Y$ are given by the following tables:
$x$ $1$ $2$ $4$
${f}_{X}(x)$ $0.35$ $0.35$ $0.3$

$y$ $2$ $3$
${f}_{Y}(y)$ $0.6$ $0.4$

Now, we can compute the expected values for $X$ and $Y:$ $$ \begin{aligned}\text{E}[X] & ={\sum }_{i=1}^{n}{x}_{i}\,{f}_{X}({x}_{i}) \\ & =1\cdot 0.35+2\cdot 0.35+4\cdot 0.3 \\ & =0.35+0.7+1.2 \\ & =2.25\end{aligned} $$ $$ \begin{aligned}\text{E}[Y] & ={\sum }_{i=1}^{n}{y}_{i}\,{f}_{Y}({y}_{i}) \\ & =2\cdot 0.6+3\cdot 0.4 \\ & =1.2+1.2 \\ & =2.4.\end{aligned} $$ Finally, using the properties of expectation, we obtain $$ \begin{aligned}\text{E}[2X-3Y] & =2\,\text{E}[X]-3\,\text{E}[Y] \\ & =2(2.25)-3(2.4) \\ & =4.5-7.2 \\ & =-2.7.\end{aligned} $$
